title: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) History Specification
subtitle: Option 33: The USA, 1954–75: conflict at home and abroad

exam_structure.overview: Section A tests source inference (4m) and causation (12m). Section B tests historical interpretations and contemporary source utility (36m) plus 4 marks for SPaG.

sections.title: Key topic 1: The development of the civil rights movement, 1954–60

topics.title: 1. The position of Black Americans in the early 1950s
points: Segregation, discrimination and voting rights in the Southern states.
The work of civil rights organisations, including the NAACP and CORE.

topics.title: 2. Developments in education
points: Reasons for, key features and significance of the Brown v. Topeka case (1954).
Reasons for, key features and significance of the events at Little Rock High School (1957).

topics.title: 3. The Montgomery Bus Boycott and its impact, 1955–60
points: Causes and events of the Montgomery Bus Boycott. The significance of Rosa Parks.
Reasons for the success and importance of the boycott. The Supreme Court ruling. The Civil Rights Act (1957).
The significance of the leadership of Martin Luther King. The setting up of the SCLC.

topics.title: 4. Opposition to the civil rights movement
points: The Ku Klux Klan and violence, including the murder of Emmet Till in 1955.
Opposition to desegregation in the South, including the ‘Dixiecrats’ and the setting up of White Citizens’ Councils.

sections.title: Key topic 2: Protest, progress and radicalism, 1960–75

topics.title: 1. Developments, 1960–62
points: The significance of Greensboro and the sit-in movement.
Reasons for, key features and significance of the Freedom Riders, including Ku Klux Klan violence and the Anniston bomb (1961).
The James Meredith case (1962).

topics.title: 2. Peaceful protests and their impact, 1963–65
points: King and the peace marches of 1963 in Birmingham and Washington.
Freedom Summer and the Mississippi murders.
The impact of peaceful protest and the roles of Presidents Kennedy and Johnson in the passage of the Civil Rights Act (1964).   Selma and the Voting Rights Act (1965).

topics.title: 3. Malcolm X and Black Power, 1963–70
points: Malcolm X, his beliefs, methods and involvement with the Black Muslims. His later change of attitude and assassination.
Reasons for the emergence of Black Power. The significance of Stokely Carmichael and the 1968 Mexico Olympics.
The methods and achievements of the Black Panther movement.

topics.title: 4. The civil rights movement, 1965–75
points: The riots of 1965–67 and the Kerner Report (1968).
King’s campaign in the North. The assassination of Martin Luther King and its impact.
The extent of progress in civil rights by 1975.

sections.title: Key topic 3: US involvement in the Vietnam War, 1954–75

topics.title: 1. Reasons for US involvement in the conflict in Vietnam, 1954–63
points: Reasons for greater US involvement under Eisenhower, including the domino theory and weaknesses of the Diem government.
Greater involvement under Kennedy, including the overthrow of Diem and the Strategic Hamlet Program.

topics.title: 2. Escalation of the conflict under Johnson
points: Reasons for the escalation of the conflict and increased US involvement in Vietnam, including the increasing threat of the Vietcong and the Gulf of Tonkin incident (1964).

topics.title: 3. The nature of the conflict in Vietnam, 1964–68
points: The guerrilla tactics used by the Vietcong.
The methods used by the USA, including Search and Destroy, Operation Rolling Thunder and chemical weapons.
The key features and significance of the Tet Offensive, 1968.

topics.title: 4. Changes under Nixon, 1969–73
points: The key features of Vietnamisation. Reasons for its failure.
The Nixon Doctrine and the withdrawal of US troops.
Attacks on Cambodia (1970)  and Laos (1971), and the bombing of North Vietnam (1972).

sections.title: Key topic 4: Reactions to, and the end of, US involvement in

topics.title: 1. Opposition to the war
points: Reasons for the growth of opposition, including the student movement, TV and media coverage of the war and the draft system.
Public reaction to the My Lai Massacre (1968). The trial of Lt. Calley.
The Kent State University shootings (1970).

topics.title: 2. Support for the war
points: Reasons for support for the war, including the fear of communism.
The ‘hard hats’ and the ‘silent majority’.

topics.title: 3. The peace process and end of the war
points: Reasons for, and key features of, the peace negotiations (1972–73).
The significance of the Paris Peace Agreement (1973).
The economic and human costs of the war for the USA.

topics.title: 4. Reasons for the failure of the USA in Vietnam
points: The strengths of North Vietnam, including the significance of Russian and Chinese support, Vietcong tactics and the Ho Chi Minh Trail.
The weaknesses of the US armed forces. The failure of US tactics.
The impact of opposition to the war in the USA.
